<div id="S6.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first compare policies within the shared production environment to examine
the effect of task-specific training without changing the tool pipeline.
We report task performance and policy-generation cost for each evaluated policy variant
in Table <a href="#S6.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 6.2 Policy Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Task-specific performance.</span>
WeVisCut improves the Overall Score from 74.5 to 90.5 over its Qwen3.5-9B
initialization, a gain of 16.0 points, with improvements in all five metrics.
The gains extend beyond successful delivery to script fidelity and visual
grounding, as SCF and VNSM increase by 18.6 and 15.4 points, respectively.
By comparison, the unadapted models show less uniform improvements over the
9B base policy. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B gains 9.0 points on ERY but loses 2.5 points on
VNSM, illustrating that delivery success does not necessarily imply better
visual–narration alignment. WeVisCut also obtains higher means on all five
metrics than Qwen3.5-397B-A17B and Gemini 3.1 Pro.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.SS2.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Comparison with Claude Opus 5.</span>
WeVisCut achieves an Overall Score of 90.5, compared with 89.9 for Claude
Opus 5. Its mean scores are higher on four metrics and slightly lower on
VNSM, with no component differing by more than 1.3 points. Yet it uses
2,377 generated tokens per successful output minute, compared with 78,763
for Claude Opus 5, or approximately one thirty-third as many. Relative to
its base policy, WeVisCut also reduces token usage from 11,883 while
maintaining 3.1 tool calls per successful output minute. These results
show that the task-adapted 9B WeVisCut policy achieves mean task scores close
to those of Claude Opus 5 at substantially lower generation cost. We next
examine quality and cost in complete editing workflows with each system’s native tools.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">

runs, and Overall is the equal-weight mean of the component means. Native

</figure>
<div id="S6.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We next evaluate whether the gains persist when each editor uses its own
tools and orchestration. In Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.3 End-to-End System Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, we compare WeVisCut with Crayotter and VideoAgent using identical task inputs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">WeVisCut achieves the highest mean score on all five metrics, with an Overall
Score of 90.5 compared with 84.9 for Crayotter and 82.5 for VideoAgent.
The improvements cover both semantic fidelity and execution quality. This pattern indicates consistent gains across content selection, temporal
planning, execution stability, and final delivery.
For example, relative to Crayotter, SCF and VNSM each improve by 6.8 points,
alongside higher plan realization, long-horizon consistency, and rendering
yield. The advantage observed in the shared environment therefore also holds
for these complete editing workflows.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These gains are accompanied by lower end-to-end costs. For each successful
output minute, WeVisCut requires 2.1 wall-clock minutes, compared with 8.6 for
Crayotter and 10.4 for VideoAgent. The corresponding estimated monetary costs
are $0.09, $0.97, and $0.58, respectively. Both measures include
unsuccessful attempts. Note that these costs reflect the complete native
workflows, rather than the efficiency of an isolated model or tool.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.4 </span>Training Stage Analysis</h3>

<figure id="S6.T3" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 3: </span>Cumulative training-stage analysis with a fixed Qwen3.5-9B backbone

are mean<math id="S6.T3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math>standard deviation across five runs on the 100 held-out tasks.

<figure id="S6.F5" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.38352v1/wedirector_three_metrics_ieee_cvpr.svg" id="S6.F5.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/129;" width="476" height="129"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 5: </span>Cumulative training progression for (a) SCF, (b) VNSM, and (c) LHC.
OPD and RL denote Guided-OPD and <span id="S6.F5.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RCF-DAPO</span>, respectively. Error bars show
standard deviations across five evaluation runs on the 100 held-out tasks.
Horizontal lines show Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, and Claude Opus 5
under the shared tool environment. Results at these checkpoints on all
five metrics are shown in Table <a href="#S6.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 6.4 Training Stage Analysis ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To examine how the training phases in Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Training WeVisCut ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> contribute to the final policy,
we evaluate successive checkpoints in Table <a href="#S6.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 6.4 Training Stage Analysis ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>.
The backbone, data split, tools, decoding configuration, and rendering budget
remain fixed. Each checkpoint adds the next training stage to the preceding
one, allowing us to track the cumulative gains across the three training phases.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In Phase 1, SFT raises ERY from 70.4 to 87.6, providing the largest
stage-wise improvement in delivery reliability. This is consistent with its
role in establishing valid tool use from executable demonstrations. RFT then
adds supervision from successful student trajectories and teacher-repaired
failures. Relative to SFT alone, it improves SCF by 6.2 points and TPR by 5.7
points, indicating gains in script fidelity and plan realization beyond the
initial improvement in delivery.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Building on this initialization, Phase 2 applies Guided-OPD to mixed
teacher–student rollouts. All five metrics improve at this checkpoint,
including VNSM from 65.1 to 67.4 and ERY from 89.8 to 91.5. This pattern
suggests that Guided-OPD complements trajectory-level RFT by refining decisions
at intermediate states, where the student must continue from its own partially
correct actions rather than replaying teacher-generated contexts. These results
show further gains after distillation on states reached during policy
execution, although the aggregate metrics do not isolate failure recovery.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.SS4.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Finally, Phase 3 optimizes production decisions with <span id="S6.SS4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">RCF-DAPO</span>. SCF and
VNSM improve by another 7.4 and 7.2 points, respectively, while Overall
increases from 84.9 to 90.5. Figure <a href="#S6.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 6.4 Training Stage Analysis ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>
shows the cumulative improvements in script fidelity, visual–narration
alignment, and long-horizon consistency against the reference policies.
These comparisons measure the benefit of adding training stages in this
order, rather than the independent effects of turn guidance, snapshot
matching, or individual role rewards.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">6.5 </span>Human Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S6.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test whether the automatic gains carry over to human judgments, three qualified
annotators independently rate anonymized videos from the three systems in
Table <a href="#S6.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 6.3 End-to-End System Comparison ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> on the same 100 held-out tasks. Videos are shown individually
in random order, with scripts, source pools, and target durations fixed. The shared
tasks allow paired comparisons. Each video is rated from 1 to 5 on the six
dimensions in Table <a href="#S6.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 6.5 Human Evaluation ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S6.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 4: </span>Blinded human evaluation on 100 held-out tasks with three raters. Entries
are mean 1–5 ratings (higher is better). Overall preference is a human rating,
distinct from the Overall Score.</figcaption>

</table>
</figure>
<div id="S6.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#S6.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 6.5 Human Evaluation ‣ 6 Experiments ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, WeVisCut obtains the highest mean rating
on all six dimensions, with an overall preference of 4.56 versus 3.48 for
Crayotter and 3.46 for VideoAgent. The largest
gains occur in narrative coherence (1.23 and 1.28 points), while higher editing
smoothness and visual quality indicate that the preference is not confined to
narrative structure, consistent with the automatic comparisons. Ratings are
averaged across annotators within each task. These descriptive means do not
establish statistical significance or validate individual automatic metrics
(see Appendix <a href="#A2.SS1" title="B.1 Diagnostic Validation ‣ Appendix B Metrics and Evidence Protocol ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B.1</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We presented WeVisCut, a system for long-form script-to-video production built
around a single 9B policy shared by the orchestrator, generator, and critic.
Our four-stage data pipeline combines editing inversion and verified replay
to recover executable supervision from finished videos. Training progresses
from executable imitation to recovery learning and reward-based decision
optimization. Our 100-task benchmark connects source scripts, editing plans,
execution traces, and final videos through five complementary metrics.
The trained policy improves all five metrics over its base model and achieves
mean scores close to those of Claude Opus 5 while using approximately one thirty-third
as many generated tokens per successful output minute. Native-system
comparisons and blinded human ratings also favor WeVisCut. Broader template
coverage and more robust retrieval are needed to extend the system to a wider
range of editing tasks.</p>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</div>
</section>

Xianyi Cheng, Tianyue Ou, Yonatan Bisk, Daniel Fried, et al.

</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock">Webarena: A realistic web environment for building autonomous agents.

</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock">In <em id="bib.bib50.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">International Conference on Learning Representations</em>,
volume 2024, pages 15585–15606, 2024.

</span></li>
      
<li id="bib.bib51" class="ltx_bibitem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_role_refnum ltx_tag_bibitem">[51]</span>

long-horizon agent training.

</span>

<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Optimization and Training Details</h2>

<div id="A1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We use the notation of Sections <a href="#S3" title="3 WeVisCut Agent Framework ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and <a href="#S5" title="5 Training WeVisCut ‣ WeVisCut: The Whole Editing Room in One AgentFrom Narration to Long-Form Video" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> throughout: <math id="A1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> indexes role calls,
<math id="A1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> indexes tokens, and <math id="A1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> indexes training updates. The task input is <math id="A1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="A1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta}^{(r)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta}^{(r)}</annotation></semantics></math> is the shared policy conditioned on role <math id="A1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Executable RFT and Guided-OPD</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Replay-safe RFT.</span>
Let <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math> index the call at which the first runtime failure occurs.
A failure is recoverable when
the environment can restore the latest transaction snapshot before
<math id="A1.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t^{\star}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>t</mi><mo>⋆</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t^{\star}</annotation></semantics></math>. External side effects are executed in a sandbox or through
idempotent calls. We retain the valid prefix, provide the teacher with the
failure record and restored state, and regenerate the complete suffix.
The repaired trajectory is retained only after replay from the snapshot
passes schema, prerequisite, artifact-reference, render, duration, narration,
lint, and black-frame checks. Its quality score <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\rm RFT}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>RFT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\rm RFT}</annotation></semantics></math> also needs to
meet the development-selected minimum <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\rm RFT}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>RFT</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\rm RFT}</annotation></semantics></math>:
<math id="A1.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\rm RFT}\geq q_{\rm RFT}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>RFT</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>RFT</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\rm RFT}\geq q_{\rm RFT}</annotation></semantics></math>. Complete student successes pass the same
admission checks. Student-only and teacher-assisted records have separate
provenance tags and fixed source–task quotas. Unrecoverable cases are kept
in a class-balanced, capped hard-case pool for later rollout sampling,
with fixed mixing probability <math id="A1.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\eta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>η</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\eta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Turn-level intervention and loss routing.</span>
Following Guided-OPD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, call <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math> consists of a complete role
output <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> followed by its runtime observation <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>. At update <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A1.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\beta_{n})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi>Bernoulli</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\beta_{n})</annotation></semantics></math> selects the teacher when <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{t}=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{t}=1</annotation></semantics></math>
and the student otherwise. The selected output is executed before control
is sampled again. Both branches contribute distillation loss. We denote
the mixed rollout distribution by <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu_{n}=\pi_{\theta,\phi}^{\beta_{n}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mi>π</mi><mrow><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ϕ</mi></mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu_{n}=\pi_{\theta,\phi}^{\beta_{n}}</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϕ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi</annotation></semantics></math> are the student and frozen teacher parameters.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The models share a tokenizer. For teacher outputs, the teacher distribution
is renormalized over its <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\rm vocab}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>vocab</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\rm vocab}</annotation></semantics></math> most likely tokens, giving
<math id="A1.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{\pi}_{\phi}^{K_{\rm vocab}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>π</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>ϕ</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>vocab</mi></msub></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{\pi}_{\phi}^{K_{\rm vocab}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Student outputs use reverse KL, while
teacher outputs use this truncated forward KL:</p>
<table id="A1.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E5.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{L}_{\rm OPD}=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu_{n}}\!\left[\frac{1}{N_{\tau}}\sum_{t,j}m_{t,j}\left((1-q_{t})D_{\rm KL}(\pi_{\theta}\|\pi_{\phi})+q_{t}D_{\rm KL}(\widetilde{\pi}_{\phi}^{K_{\rm vocab}}\|\pi_{\theta})\right)_{c_{t,j}}\right]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mi>OPD</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>∼</mo><msub><mi>μ</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo>[</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub></mfrac><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></munder><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>KL</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>ϕ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>KL</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>π</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>ϕ</mi><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>vocab</mi></msub></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∥</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></msub><mo>]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}_{\rm OPD}=\mathbb{E}_{\tau\sim\mu_{n}}\!\left[\frac{1}{N_{\tau}}\sum_{t,j}m_{t,j}\left((1-q_{t})D_{\rm KL}(\pi_{\theta}\|\pi_{\phi})+q_{t}D_{\rm KL}(\widetilde{\pi}_{\phi}^{K_{\rm vocab}}\|\pi_{\theta})\right)_{c_{t,j}}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t,j}</annotation></semantics></math> contains the role context <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and all tokens preceding
position <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> in call <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>. The policies in each KL term are conditioned on
this token prefix. The mask <math id="A1.SS1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{t,j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{t,j}</annotation></semantics></math> is one for assistant tokens and zero
for input, padding, and runtime observations, and
<math id="A1.SS1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N_{\tau}=\sum_{t,j}m_{t,j}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>τ</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><msub><mi>m</mi><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N_{\tau}=\sum_{t,j}m_{t,j}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> counts supervised tokens.
Thus teacher-only trajectories also train the student. We log retained
top-<math id="A1.SS1.p3.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K_{\rm vocab}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>K</mi><mi>vocab</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K_{\rm vocab}</annotation></semantics></math> probability mass to audit truncation. This is an
efficiency variant of Guided-OPD. Step-Level OPD instead keeps trajectories
student-controlled and queries teacher targets afterward <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Teacher intervention follows</p>
<table id="A1.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{n}=\beta_{\rm start}\frac{1+\cos(\pi\min(n/T_{\rm decay},1))}{2},\qquad\beta_{\rm start}=0.8," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>n</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>start</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>min</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>decay</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>start</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8</mn></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{n}=\beta_{\rm start}\frac{1+\cos(\pi\min(n/T_{\rm decay},1))}{2},\qquad\beta_{\rm start}=0.8,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T_{\rm decay}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>T</mi><mi>decay</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T_{\rm decay}</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of updates over which intervention
decays, set to 70% of training. The remaining 30% uses student-only
rollouts. Only checkpoints evaluated without teacher intervention proceed
to RL. Guided-OPD uses a 50-call horizon with early termination, while RL
uses the 16-call deployment budget. Token limits are per-call
context/response caps, and compact state updates limit history growth.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>Role- and Context-Factored DAPO</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Optimization scope.</span>
Each trainable call records its role <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, context <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, output <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math>, observation
<math id="A1.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>o</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o</annotation></semantics></math>, and execution contract <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>u</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u</annotation></semantics></math>. Main rollouts populate a snapshot buffer.
For an orchestrator context <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>, we restore the pre-decision state,
sample alternative outputs, and execute each with the same frozen
continuation policy <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}</annotation></semantics></math>, budget, and seed set.
Here <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta_{\rm old}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta_{\rm old}</annotation></semantics></math> is the policy parameter snapshot frozen for the
current optimization iteration.
Nested generator and critic tokens are masked from the orchestrator loss.
Generator and critic contexts are also collected from current-policy
rollouts and resampled locally. Let <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> be the context distribution for
role <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> its outer loss weight. The optimized proxy is</p>
<table id="A1.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="J_{\rm proxy}=\sum_{r\in\{\rm O,G,C\}}\lambda_{r}\mathbb{E}_{c\sim\operatorname{sg}(d_{r}),z\sim\pi_{\theta}^{(r)}(\cdot\mid c)}[R^{(r)}(c,z)]." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>J</mi><mi>proxy</mi></msub><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>G</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><msub><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>sg</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>r</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo>∼</mo><mi>π</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>θ</mi></msub><msup><mrow></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∣</mo><mi>c</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J_{\rm proxy}=\sum_{r\in\{\rm O,G,C\}}\lambda_{r}\mathbb{E}_{c\sim\operatorname{sg}(d_{r}),z\sim\pi_{\theta}^{(r)}(\cdot\mid c)}[R^{(r)}(c,z)].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R^{(r)}(c,z)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>R</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>c</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R^{(r)}(c,z)</annotation></semantics></math> is the expected execution reward for output <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> in
context <math id="A1.SS2.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>c</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>, with runtime observations averaged out.
This is a conditional call-level objective. Frozen continuations and the
sampled context distribution remain part of the proxy, so it does not
provide an unbiased gradient of the terminal production return.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Matched comparison groups.</span>
For orchestrator call <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, we fix
<math id="A1.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\rm O,t}=(x,c_{t},s_{t},\mathcal{T},B_{t},\pi_{\rm cont})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒯</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>cont</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\rm O,t}=(x,c_{t},s_{t},\mathcal{T},B_{t},\pi_{\rm cont})</annotation></semantics></math>:
the task input, context, restored state, tool space, remaining budget <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>,
and continuation policy <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{\rm cont}=\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>cont</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{\rm cont}=\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}</annotation></semantics></math>.
Only the next output varies. Generator groups fix the local request,
artifact, tool, schema/version, budget, and initial state.
Critic groups also fix the defect and verification contract. Candidate
executions share paired seeds. Let <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{G}_{\kappa}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{G}_{\kappa}</annotation></semantics></math> be the group of
outputs sampled under matching conditions <math id="A1.SS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Features are mapped to their registered ranges: <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, except repair
utility in <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[-1,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[-1,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Fixed weights produce one reward per output before
group normalization. Contexts are sampled through role–task–tool quotas.
A group is accepted only if
<math id="A1.SS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{Var}_{i\in\mathcal{G}_{\kappa}}(R_{i}^{(r)})&gt;\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>Var</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒢</mi><mi>κ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{Var}_{i\in\mathcal{G}_{\kappa}}(R_{i}^{(r)})&gt;\delta</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta</annotation></semantics></math> is the minimum reward-variance threshold. Otherwise it is
resampled up to a fixed cap. Low-variance contexts remain in a coverage
queue and are revisited through executable imitation. For an accepted group,</p>
<table id="A1.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sigma_{\kappa}^{(r)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>σ</mi><mi>κ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sigma_{\kappa}^{(r)}</annotation></semantics></math> is the group reward standard deviation,
<math id="A1.SS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> stabilizes normalization, and <math id="A1.SS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{sg}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>sg</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{sg}</annotation></semantics></math> stops
gradients through group statistics. No normalization mixes roles or
unmatched contexts. Resampling emphasizes informative reward differences
and changes the sampled context distribution.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Role-specific rewards.</span>
For candidate <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> be its role output and <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="o_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>o</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">o_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> its execution
feedback. An orchestrator output is scored by continuing from snapshot <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>.
We measure progress through validated milestones:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\Phi(s)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\Phi(s)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\sum_{k}\omega_{k}I_{k}(s)}{\sum_{k}\omega_{k}},\qquad r_{\ell}^{\rm prog}=\gamma\Phi(s_{\ell+1})-\Phi(s_{\ell})," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mi>k</mi></msub><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>prog</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\sum_{k}\omega_{k}I_{k}(s)}{\sum_{k}\omega_{k}},\qquad r_{\ell}^{\rm prog}=\gamma\Phi(s_{\ell+1})-\Phi(s_{\ell}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E9"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle F_{i,t}^{\rightarrow}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle F_{i,t}^{\rightarrow}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=(1-\epsilon_{p})\operatorname{clip}\!\left(\sum_{\ell\geq t}\gamma^{\ell-t}r_{\ell}^{\rm prog},0,1\right)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.428em;" width="1.428em"><mi>clip</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></munder></mstyle><mrow><msup><mi>γ</mi><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>r</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mi>prog</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=(1-\epsilon_{p})\operatorname{clip}\!\left(\sum_{\ell\geq t}\gamma^{\ell-t}r_{\ell}^{\rm prog},0,1\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{k}(s)\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>s</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{k}(s)\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math> indicates whether unique milestone <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> holds in
state <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\omega_{k}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ω</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\omega_{k}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math> is its fixed weight, <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\gamma\leq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\gamma\leq 1</annotation></semantics></math> is the discount
factor, and <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\ell" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\ell</annotation></semantics></math> indexes subsequent calls until branch <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math> terminates. Repetition adds no
milestone credit, and later invalidation removes it. The positive margin
<math id="A1.SS2.p4.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0&lt;\epsilon_{p}&lt;1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>ϵ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0&lt;\epsilon_{p}&lt;1</annotation></semantics></math> keeps failed-branch progress below the delivery tier.
The operator <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\operatorname{clip}(\cdot,0,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\operatorname{clip}(\cdot,0,1)</annotation></semantics></math> bounds its argument to <math id="A1.SS2.p4.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">The rewards are</p>
<table id="A1.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle R_{i}^{\mathrm{O}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>O</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle R_{i}^{\mathrm{O}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=g_{{\rm del},i}[\alpha+(1-\alpha)Q_{{\rm end},i}]+(1-g_{{\rm del},i})\alpha F_{i,t}^{\rightarrow}-\lambda_{p}p_{i}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>del</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>end</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>del</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>F</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">→</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=g_{{\rm del},i}[\alpha+(1-\alpha)Q_{{\rm end},i}]+(1-g_{{\rm del},i})\alpha F_{i,t}^{\rightarrow}-\lambda_{p}p_{i},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p5.2" class="ltx_p">The delivery indicator <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{{\rm del},i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mrow><mi>del</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{{\rm del},i}</annotation></semantics></math> is one only if termination, schema,
prerequisite, artifact, and loop checks pass and final quality
<math id="A1.SS2.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{{\rm end},i}\geq q_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mi>end</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><mo>≥</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>min</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{{\rm end},i}\geq q_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q_{\min}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>min</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q_{\min}</annotation></semantics></math> is the minimum delivery
quality. Otherwise it is zero. A legal stop below this threshold is
premature, recorded by the indicator <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{i}\in\{0,1\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{i}\in\{0,1\}</annotation></semantics></math>.
The parameter <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> weights delivery and progress credit
relative to final quality, and <math id="A1.SS2.p5.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{p}\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{p}\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math> weights the premature-stop penalty.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Final quality combines a rule score and a sampled render audit:
<math id="A1.SS2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\rm end}=(1-w_{a})Q_{\rm rule}+w_{a}Q_{\rm audit}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>end</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>rule</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>audit</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\rm end}=(1-w_{a})Q_{\rm rule}+w_{a}Q_{\rm audit}</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{\rm rule},Q_{\rm audit}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>rule</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>audit</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{\rm rule},Q_{\rm audit}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{a}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>a</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{a}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> is the fixed
audit weight. The six rule features are plan
coverage, spotlight-decoration coverage, inspection coverage, plan hygiene,
completion, and efficiency, weighted 0.353, 0.186, 0.179, 0.144, 0.081, and
0.057. The render audit scores visual impact and clarity. Thus these six
weights apply to rule features, with the audit blended separately.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Generator features <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{k}^{\mathrm{G}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{k}^{\mathrm{G}}</annotation></semantics></math> measure schema validity, grounding,
requirement coverage, and downstream usability using deterministic checks
and a frozen tool-specific rubric. All features are set to zero for an
invalid schema. Critic features <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\rm diag},i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>diag</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\rm diag},i}</annotation></semantics></math> and
<math id="A1.SS2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\rm verify},i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>verify</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\rm verify},i}</annotation></semantics></math> score diagnosis and verification,
and <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{{\rm unnecessary},i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mrow><mi>unnecessary</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{{\rm unnecessary},i}</annotation></semantics></math> penalizes unnecessary repair.
The coefficients <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{k}^{\mathrm{G}},w_{d},w_{r},w_{v},w_{u}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>w</mi><mi>k</mi><mi>G</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>d</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>u</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{k}^{\mathrm{G}},w_{d},w_{r},w_{v},w_{u}</annotation></semantics></math> are fixed feature weights.
Here <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the diagnosis provided by critic output <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>. For a diagnosis
<math id="A1.SS2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>, controlled repair utility is</p>
<table id="A1.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="U_{\rm repair}(d)=\frac{1}{|\Xi|}\sum_{\xi\in\Xi}\left[Q(A_{\rm fix}(d;\xi))-Q(A_{\rm fix}(d_{0};\xi))\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>U</mi><mi>repair</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false" rspace="0em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>ξ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ξ</mi></mrow></munder><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>fix</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>fix</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">U_{\rm repair}(d)=\frac{1}{|\Xi|}\sum_{\xi\in\Xi}\left[Q(A_{\rm fix}(d;\xi))-Q(A_{\rm fix}(d_{0};\xi))\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(11)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p7.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A_{\rm fix}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>A</mi><mi>fix</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A_{\rm fix}</annotation></semantics></math> is a frozen repair executor with identical tool version
and budget, <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is an empty diagnosis, <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Xi</annotation></semantics></math> is a paired seed set, and
<math id="A1.SS2.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> maps repair results to a fixed quality score in <math id="A1.SS2.p7.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus utility measures the
improvement over the empty-diagnosis baseline under controlled execution.
The training judge, rubric, prompt, and version hash are frozen and
independent of the held-out evaluator. Rule and judge scores are logged
separately.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A1.SS2.p8.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">DAPO update.</span>
Let <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{B}_{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{B}_{r}</annotation></semantics></math> be the candidate batch for role <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="A1.SS2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}</annotation></semantics></math> the model-authored token positions in output <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>z</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>.
For token <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, the policy probability ratio is
<math id="A1.SS2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho_{i,j}=\pi_{\theta}(z_{i,j}\mid c_{i},z_{i,&lt;j})/\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}(z_{i,j}\mid c_{i},z_{i,&lt;j})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>θ</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><msub><mi>θ</mi><mi>old</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo fence="true" lspace="0em" rspace="0em">∣</mo><mrow><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>z</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mphantom></mphantom></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho_{i,j}=\pi_{\theta}(z_{i,j}\mid c_{i},z_{i,&lt;j})/\pi_{\theta_{\rm old}}(z_{i,j}\mid c_{i},z_{i,&lt;j})</annotation></semantics></math>,
where <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="c_{i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>c</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is the candidate’s input context.
We use DAPO’s asymmetric Clip-Higher interval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">43</a>]</cite>, with
<math id="A1.SS2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{\rm low}=0.20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>low</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{\rm low}=0.20</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon_{\rm high}=0.28" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>ε</mi><mi>high</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.28</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon_{\rm high}=0.28</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
<table id="A1.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A1.Ex4"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\ell_{i,j}^{(r)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\ell_{i,j}^{(r)}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.Ex4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\min\!\left(\rho_{i,j}A_{i}^{(r)},\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,j},0.8,1.28)A_{i}^{(r)}\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:1.653em;" width="1.653em"><mi>min</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>clip</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mn>0.8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1.28</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>A</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\min\!\left(\rho_{i,j}A_{i}^{(r)},\operatorname{clip}(\rho_{i,j},0.8,1.28)A_{i}^{(r)}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A1.E12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{J}_{\rm RCF\text{-}DAPO}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒥</mi><mrow><mi>RCF</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>-</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>DAPO</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{J}_{\rm RCF\text{-}DAPO}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A1.E12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{r}\lambda_{r}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}_{r}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}}\ell_{i,j}^{(r)}}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}_{r}}|\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}|}\right]." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mi>r</mi></munder></mstyle><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mpadded style="width:0.497em;" width="0.497em"><mi>𝔼</mi></mpadded><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.167em">∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>∈</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></msub><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>r</mi></msub></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em" stretchy="false">|</mo><msubsup><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><mi>i</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>r</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{r}\lambda_{r}\,\mathbb{E}\!\left[\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}_{r}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}}\ell_{i,j}^{(r)}}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{B}_{r}}|\mathcal{M}_{i}^{(r)}|}\right].</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">Token losses are aggregated within each role before applying the outer
weights <math id="A1.SS2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\rm O}=\lambda_{\rm G}=\lambda_{\rm C}=1/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>G</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\rm O}=\lambda_{\rm G}=\lambda_{\rm C}=1/3</annotation></semantics></math>.
The old policy is synchronized once per optimization iteration.
We use neither dual clipping nor a loss-side KL term.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS2.p9" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="A1.SS2.p9.1" class="ltx_p">For generated token count <math id="A1.SS2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>L</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L</annotation></semantics></math>, let <math id="A1.SS2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\rm soft}&lt;L_{\rm cap}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>cap</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\rm soft}&lt;L_{\rm cap}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the
no-penalty threshold and generation hard cap. For non-truncated responses,
soft overlong shaping is</p>
<table id="A1.E13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A1.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p_{\rm len}(L)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;L\leq L_{\rm soft},\\
-\lambda_{\rm len}\dfrac{L-L_{\rm soft}}{L_{\rm cap}-L_{\rm soft}},&amp;L_{\rm soft}&lt;L&lt;L_{\rm cap}.\end{cases}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>p</mi><mi>len</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>L</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mtable columnspacing="5pt" displaystyle="true" rowspacing="0pt"><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr><mtr><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>len</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>L</mi><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>cap</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow></mtd><mtd class="ltx_align_left" columnalign="left"><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>L</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>cap</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow></mtd></mtr></mtable></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p_{\rm len}(L)=\begin{cases}0,&amp;L\leq L_{\rm soft},\\
-\lambda_{\rm len}\dfrac{L-L_{\rm soft}}{L_{\rm cap}-L_{\rm soft}},&amp;L_{\rm soft}&lt;L&lt;L_{\rm cap}.\end{cases}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A1.SS2.p9.2" class="ltx_p">We set <math id="A1.SS2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="L_{\rm soft}=L_{\rm cap}-2{,}048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>soft</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>L</mi><mi>cap</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>2,048</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">L_{\rm soft}=L_{\rm cap}-2{,}048</annotation></semantics></math> and the length-penalty weight
<math id="A1.SS2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda_{\rm len}=0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>λ</mi><mi>len</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda_{\rm len}=0.1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Responses reaching the hard cap are replaced before an eight-candidate
group is formed. If the resampling cap is reached first, the group is
dropped. Truncated responses enter neither rewards, group statistics,
nor policy loss. Role-wise gradient norms and pairwise cosine similarities
are logged, since outer loss weights control scale but do not eliminate
shared-parameter gradient conflict.</p>
</div>
